input.rationale: The compaction question's own discriminator is now answered by source inspection, and the declared incomplete work is the failure side; this update records precisely what would still change the judgment for that question instead of leaving the answered discriminator in place.

investigations.discriminator: Settled by inspection: no compaction path exists (handle methods, Command variants and the actor's calls into the core were all checked). What would still change the judgment: (i) executing the failure side - a Storage implementation whose write returns Err, driven through the actor - to see whether the core's fatal write error really ends the actor task and whether every caller-visible endpoint then collapses to AppendError::Shutdown / RuntimeProposeErr::Shutdown (as the source chain implies) or whether the layer surfaces something distinguishable, which would narrow the attribution part of the account; and (ii) any documentation stating that compaction is deliberately out of scope for the layer, which would limit the first part to a capability gap rather than an omitted duty.

investigations.question: Can a full, undrained RuntimeConfig event channel (a subscribed but unread subscribe_events() receiver) stop the single actor task, and with it the node's whole consensus participation - ticks, message handling and every Command reply?
investigations.hypothesis: detect_and_emit_events awaits event_tx.send for every observed transition and is awaited inside the run loop's tick arm, so once the bounded event channel is full the actor task parks inside the tick arm: no further tick() (leader election heartbeat, resend and flush timers), no incoming-message handling, and no Command reply (not even the documented append_notify Timeout, which drain_notifiers would have produced).
investigations.discriminator: Two runs of the same 3-node in-process cluster that differ only in whether an unread event receiver exists: (A) nobody reads events at all (only the receiver the handle itself holds from spawn_actor); (B) a per-node consumer task reads events until a flag is set and then keeps the receiver but stops reading. The hypothesis predicts both variants park the actor after event_capacity transitions; the construction observations contradict that for (B), so the decisive next information is whether the sender in (B) actually observes a full channel - i.e. the real capacity/state of the event channel (Sender::capacity / try_send from a probe) and whether events are still being produced at that moment, rather than a further variant of the freeze symptom.

history.question: Can a full, undrained RuntimeConfig event channel (a subscribed but unread subscribe_events() receiver) stop the single actor task, and with it the node's whole consensus participation - ticks, message handling and every Command reply?
history.hypothesis: detect_and_emit_events awaits event_tx.send for every observed transition and is awaited inside the run loop's tick arm, so once the bounded event channel is full the actor task parks inside the tick arm: no further tick() (leader election heartbeat, resend and flush timers), no incoming-message handling, and no Command reply (not even the documented append_notify Timeout, which drain_notifiers would have produced).
history.discriminator: An execution that subscribes without draining on every node of a live in-process cluster: if the actor task is parked on the event send, Command round-trips never complete and a fresh append_notify never reaches its 300ms Timeout endpoint, while the same cluster with the same event_capacity but a draining receiver keeps answering commands and decides the same entry.

investigations.question: In the core Sequence Paxos, if a follower's Accepted reply (or the leader's AcceptDecide) is lost, does any timer-driven or self-initiated mechanism restore the leader's knowledge of that acceptance, or does a quorum-accepted entry stay undecided until an unrelated new proposal arrives?
investigations.hypothesis: There is no repair for this direction: resend_messages_leader in Phase::Accept only resends a pending StopSign/its decide and re-Prepares peers that are not promised, and resend_messages_follower in Phase::Accept is an empty arm, so a lost Accepted is never retried by either side; the leader's decision only re-evaluates on a later handle_accepted, i.e. only when some follower accepts something new, which requires an unrelated proposal.
investigations.discriminator: A deterministic in-process simulation (real OmniPaxos instances with a memory storage, manual message delivery and logical ticks): elect a leader, propose one entry, let the follower accept it, drop only that follower's Accepted, then keep ticking and delivering for a fair window with no new proposals, and compare the leader's decided_idx against a control run in which the same message is delivered. If the entry stays undecided in the drop case while both the leader's own acceptance and the follower's accepted_idx show a quorum, the loss is repaired by nothing in that interval; if the entry becomes decided without the message or without a new proposal, the hypothesis is refuted.

investigations.question: Can append_notify resolve Ok(idx) for an entry that was never decided at idx - specifically when the index the call was assigned is later occupied by a different entry - and is the documented Superseded heuristic therefore shadowed by the index-only check?
investigations.hypothesis: drain_notifiers matches the index-based arm `Some((idx, _)) if idx <= decided` before the ballot-based Superseded arm, so a call whose assigned index becomes decided by a different entry resolves Ok(idx); the actor cannot detect the substitution because Entry is only Clone + Debug, and the Superseded heuristic therefore cannot fire once the decided index covers the assignment.
investigations.discriminator: Boundary measured, execution 78c53df3891643edafaa4f10d60ea5d1: with the caller's entry adopted by the following leader the same call is truthful (event 2 `adopted_entry_resolution` a_entry_at_index_1_is_own true, resolution Ok(1)), with it unadopted the call is false (event 1 `overwritten_index_resolution` a_entry_at_index_1_is_own false, resolution Ok(1)). What would still change the judgment: a construction in which the caller's entry was accepted by a quorum and is nevertheless replaced at its index, which the prepare-phase adoption path (Promise log_sync / take_max_promise_sync) argues against, or a cadence at which the resolution tick lands between the promise change and the re-synchronization.

history.question: Can append_notify resolve Ok(idx) for an entry that was never decided at idx - specifically when the index the call was assigned is later occupied by a different entry - and is the documented Superseded heuristic therefore shadowed by the index-only check?
history.hypothesis: drain_notifiers matches on the pending item's assignment in the order `Some((idx, _)) if idx <= decided` first and `Some((idx, ballot)) if ballot < cur_ballot` second, so once the node's decided index covers the assigned index the call resolves Ok(idx) even if leadership moved on and the entry was overwritten; the Ok contract (await its decided log index, and the documented usage 'durably decided at log idx') is then false, and the Superseded heuristic that was written for exactly this leadership-change case never fires.
history.discriminator: Construction that isolates the assigned index from its entry: node A is the leader and accepts its own entry at index 1 with its outgoing and incoming traffic cut, so the entry never leaves A; nodes B and C then elect B and decide index 1 with B's own entry; A is let back in and re-syncs, truncating its log to B's and raising its decided index to 1. If A's pending call resolves Ok(1) while the entry at index 1 on A is B's entry and not A's, the index-only check is a false completion; if it resolves Superseded instead, the hypothesis is refuted.

history.question: Can append_notify resolve Ok(idx) for an entry that was never decided at idx - specifically when the index the call was assigned is later occupied by a different entry - and is the documented Superseded heuristic therefore shadowed by the index-only check?
history.hypothesis: drain_notifiers matches the index-based arm `Some((idx, _)) if idx <= decided` before the ballot-based Superseded arm, so a call whose assigned index becomes decided by a different entry resolves Ok(idx); the actor cannot detect the substitution because Entry is only Clone + Debug, and the Superseded heuristic therefore cannot fire once the decided index covers the assignment.
history.discriminator: Witnessed so far: an entry accepted only locally (isolated node, never replicated) whose assigned index is later covered by a different entry's decision, after which the call resolves Ok(idx) while the entry at idx is not the caller's. The next information that would change the judgment is whether the same false completion is reachable when the caller's entry was actually accepted by a write quorum: the following leader adopts a quorum-accepted value through the prepare-phase Promise log_sync and take_max_promise_sync before it syncs anyone (leader.rs:257-285, follower.rs:13-51), so the expectation is that such an entry cannot be replaced at its index and the Ok arm would then be truthful; that expectation is testable by replicating the entry to a quorum before cutting the leader and letting the next leader sync from a node that accepted it.

investigations.question: Can a user of the omnipaxos_runtime actor layer reach the core's documented log compaction (OmniPaxos::trim / OmniPaxos::snapshot) at all - does any handle method, any Command variant or any internal call the actor makes into the core provide that path?
investigations.hypothesis: No path exists: spawn_actor consumes the OmniPaxos instance by value, the handle keeps only channels and a capacity (no accessor for the instance and no trim/snapshot method), the actor's Command enum has no compaction variant, and nothing in the actor calls op.trim()/op.snapshot(), so a runtime-only user cannot bound the log's growth.
investigations.discriminator: Source inspection of all three places a path could exist: every public method on OmniPaxosHandle, every Command variant in the actor protocol, and every call the actor makes into the core. Finding a compaction command, a handle method or any internal call reaching trim/snapshot would refute the hypothesis; documentation stating that compaction is deliberately out of scope would limit it to a capability gap rather than an omission.

result.summary: Recorded the compaction question's state precisely rather than starting a probe I could not finish in the remaining budget: the path-absence side is settled by inspection (handle methods, Command variants and the actor's calls into the core were all checked, so no compaction reaches the instance the actor consumed), and the discriminator now names exactly what would still change the judgment — (i) executing the failure side, a Storage implementation whose write returns Err driven through the actor, to see whether the core's fatal write error really ends the actor task and whether every caller-visible endpoint then collapses to AppendError::Shutdown / RuntimeProposeErr::Shutdown as the source chain implies, or whether the layer surfaces something distinguishable (which would narrow the attribution part), and (ii) any documentation stating compaction is deliberately out of scope for the layer (which would limit the first part to a capability gap). I checked the snapshot's atomic-storage test file for a reusable failing-storage wrapper before deciding; it does not provide one in a directly reusable form, so that probe remains the declared next action rather than a rushed guess. Final position of the audit, unchanged by this turn: four findings — the actor layer's event egress parks the loop and stalls the cluster at capacities 8/64/1024 under a corrected transport (receipts ff4511e8, 76557a28, bbff5b4c, with a 21.69s retrospective bound and the superseded transport-jam run kept as an excluded cause); the core has no timer-driven repair for a lost Accepted, now measured at two and three nodes with quorum-critical losses (receipts 092538c6, 9f3f25cc, one open accounting question closed by explanation); append_notify can resolve Ok for an index occupied by another entry, bounded by measurement to unadopted entries (receipts 743518e2, 78c53df3); and the actor layer owns the instance but offers no compaction path, with the panic-to-Shutdown attribution chain and the repository's own compaction documentation as the norm (source-settled, failure side not yet exercised).
